author: Diptanu Choudhury
text: We are seeing backlash against sandboxes for primarily a couple of reasons - vendors don't support users to overcommit compute. You can't pay for N cores and overcommit the number of sandboxes that are run on those cores. In reality agents don't uniformly use resources during [quote: Arlan on code hallucinations & data freshness]
suggestedEngagement: Agree and add nuance: agent workloads are fundamentally bursty — unlike always-on services, they spike hard then go idle, so overcommit is the natural fit. Ask how they think vendors should price it.
Share experience: at scale you can colocate agent runs that have different burst profiles to smooth out utilization — curious if tensorlake is pursuing that approach.
Challenge/extend: vendors may resist overcommit because of noisy-neighbor risk on CPU-intensive sandboxes — how does diptanu think about isolation guarantees when you overcommit?
